clue.text: Bird doesn't have white on body initially

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the body letter comes first
initially asks for only the opening letter of the word body

parts.note: to lack something is not to have it
wan means pale, white in the face

explanation.surface: A bird described as having no white plumage on its body, starting from the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white' looks like a plumage colour but means pale; 'on' in an across clue puts the body letter first.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark Australian waterfowl species is a kind of bird.

clue.text: A crust brought home, something for breakfast?

definitions.meaning: a crust here is a living, as in bringing home the ..., earning money for the household
cured pork rashers are a breakfast staple

explanation.surface: Someone bringing home a pie crust, wondering whether it will do for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'bring home the bacon' is to earn a living, which is what 'a crust' means in the idiom 'earn a crust'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning a crust and bringing home the bacon are both idioms for winning one's livelihood; the rashers are also a breakfast food.

clue.text: Sky entertainment broadcast twice?

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
twice asks for a second word meaning broadcast: to show a programme is also to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A television entertainment broadcast twice on Sky, the satellite channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' asks for two different synonyms of 'broadcast' side by side. 'Sky' looks like the British satellite TV company but means the actual sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying display of aircraft is entertainment performed up in the sky.

clue.text: Old country dancing champ with a uke

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the letters of champ, a and uke are rearranged

explanation.surface: A champion from a former nation dancing while strumming a ukulele.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges CHAMP + A + UKE.
explanation.definitionFit: The name Cambodia bore under the Khmer Rouge, a former state name no longer used.

clue.text: Hurriedly get down street in time for call from an admirer

parts.note: to wolf food is to gulp it down fast

indicators.note: in tells us the street abbreviation goes inside the word for time

parts.note: a while is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone rushing down a street in time to hear an admirer's call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get down' suggests descending, but here it means swallowing food.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-note whistle aimed at an attractive passer-by is an admiring call.

clue.text: Head, as once compared with bonce?

definitions.text: Head, as once compared with bonce?

parts.words: Head, as once compared with bonce
parts.note: bonce is modern British slang for the head; the clue asks for an older slang word for the same thing

explanation.surface: A query about how an old word for the head stacks up against the slang 'bonce'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonce' is current British slang for the head; the answer is the older slang term, now dated.
explanation.definitionFit: An old slang word for the head, from the days before skull-slang like bonce took over.

clue.text: Hard to fake passport, perhaps?

parts.note: to rig a result is to fake it
a passport is one example of an ID document

explanation.surface: Forging a passport is said to be difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks passport as an example of ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard in the sense of stiff and unbending, not easily flexed.

clue.text: Collapse, having covered new dispute

indicators.note: the word for collapse wraps around the abbreviation for new

parts.note: to ruin is to fall to pieces, collapse

explanation.surface: Something collapsed after a cover-up of fresh information.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is an informal word for a quarrel or clash with someone.

clue.text: Start doing the Mexican wave as Mardi Gras ends

indicators.note: ends asks for the final letter of every one of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A crowd begins a Mexican wave as the Mardi Gras carnival draws to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' looks like it refers only to Mardi Gras, but it takes the last letter of every word from 'doing' to 'Gras'.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means an origin or beginning, as in the first book of the Bible.

clue.text: Old soldier wrongly arrested, trial's beginning

indicators.note: wrongly signals the letters of arrested are put in a different order
beginning asks for the first letter of trial's

explanation.surface: An elderly veteran is wrongly arrested, and the trial is starting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges ARRESTED; 'beginning' supplies T.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterans of the British 7th Armoured Division in the North African campaign of WWII were nicknamed after a desert rodent.

clue.text: Sweet area in high ground in Israel

indicators.note: in places the area abbreviation inside the mountain's name

parts.note: Mount Carmel is a mountain range in northern Israel

explanation.surface: A pleasant spot on a hill in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective describing the area but is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy toffee-like confection made from heated sugar is a sweet.

clue.text: Hand off your head

definitions.meaning: a hand is a cluster of the fruit growing together on one stem
off your head means crazy, mad

explanation.definitionFit: A bunch of the fruit is called a hand, and going crazy is slang for being mad.

clue.text: Indian leader once close to Australian? Sorry sport!

indicators.note: close to asks for the final letter of Australian

parts.note: Eh? is what you say instead of Sorry? when you didn't hear
RU stands for rugby union

explanation.surface: A former Indian leader, friendly with an Australian, apologises to a good sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' reads as 'near' but means the last letter; 'Sorry?' is a request to repeat, i.e. Eh?
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister, a past political leader.

clue.text: Covering land, more sensible to find rake

indicators.note: the word for more sensible wraps around the country's name

parts.note: wiser means more sensible
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: Covering ground, a wise person finds a garden rake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' looks like a garden tool but is an old word for a dissolute man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeker, especially a man who chases women.

clue.text: Old film this new?

parts.note: an old Chaplin film whose title describes the present day as new; the clue plays on old versus new

explanation.surface: Asking whether an old film could be called new.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaplin's 1936 film has a title that means 'present-day era', which is a paradox for an old film.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charlie Chaplin comedy from 1936 is an old film whose title describes the present era.

clue.text: Head for East End district

definitions.meaning: the front end of a ship is its head
An area of the East End of London

explanation.surface: Someone heading for a district in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: The forward part of a vessel is its head, and Bow is a district in east London.

clue.text: Country music to sing, get down on it!

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so blue comes first

parts.note: something that gets you down makes you blue, depressed
to sing or grass is criminal slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: A country song urging listeners to sing and get down on the dancefloor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sing' and 'grass' are both British slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of American country music from Appalachia, played on banjo and fiddle.

clue.text: Owner of scissors locks cupboard

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair
a dresser is a kitchen cupboard with shelves

explanation.surface: A scissors owner locks them in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' looks like a verb but is a noun, hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylist who cuts hair would own professional scissors.

clue.text: Timeless principle underlining conclusions of article on gland

definitions.note: gland is a noun but the answer is an adjective; the answer describes ductless glands

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits under the first
conclusions of asks for the final letters of article and on
timeless means the letter for time is removed

parts.note: a doctrine is a principle or belief

explanation.surface: A principle underlining the conclusions of an article about a gland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' takes T out of the principle, leaving DOCRINE. 'gland' stands in for an adjective here: the answer describes a kind of gland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ductless hormone-producing organs like the thyroid form a body system named with this adjective, which qualifies a gland.

clue.text: Lawless dunce, rather foolish

indicators.note: foolish suggests the letters of dunce and rather are being silly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dunce who is lawless rather than merely foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolish' rearranges DUNCE RATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a charter, a group operates outside formal rules, so lawless.

clue.text: Focused money on roulette choice

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, money
a roulette player can bet on red or black

explanation.surface: A gambler with money focused on a red bet at roulette.
explanation.definitionFit: Being concentrated in the middle, focused and balanced.

clue.text: First back gets the trophy

indicators.note: back tells us the word for first is read backwards

parts.note: top means first, best

explanation.surface: The winner who comes first gets the trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup awarded as a prize, slang for a trophy.

clue.text: Fictitious horse in seasonal performance, male

indicators.note: in puts the horse letter inside the seasonal show

parts.note: a panto is a British Christmas pantomime show
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A pantomime horse played by a man in a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is the drug heroin, H. A panto is the British family pantomime staged at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory or imaginary, existing only in the mind, is fictitious.

clue.text: Get down good clue: often nothing lost after editing?

indicators.note: after editing, the letters of clue and often are rearranged
lost means the letter for nothing is taken out

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A setter told to kneel because their clue often loses nothing in editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes O from CLUEOFTEN; 'after editing' rearranges the rest to ENUFLECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend the knee as a mark of respect is to get down.

clue.text: Humbug, some confectionery

definitions.meaning: humbug here means nonsense, evasive talk
a soft sweet made from sugar, butter and milk

explanation.walkthrough: Humbug is also a British boiled mint sweet, which makes the second meaning look like the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive nonsense and a soft sugary sweet share this name.

clue.text: Stroke head and tail of cougar with tool

indicators.note: head and tail of asks for the first and last letters of cougar

parts.note: an awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.surface: Stroking a cougar's head and tail with a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' looks like a verb of petting but is a swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Front swimming style, also called freestyle, is a stroke.

clue.text: Number fifty in uprising, communist

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads from bottom to top, reversing the letters

parts.note: nine is a number
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people join an uprising led by a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Bolshevik Revolution and founded the Soviet state, a famous communist.

clue.text: Something going too far in film? Cut!

definitions.text: Something going too far in film
definitions.meaning: the 1977 war film A Bridge Too Far: in its title, the thing that goes too far
to cut a text is to shorten it

explanation.surface: A director shouting 'Cut!' at a stunt that went too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut!' looks like a director's call, but it is a verb meaning shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a book or speech is to cut it; the war film's title also supplies the words.

clue.text: Spirit in character needing no introduction

indicators.note: no introduction means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: one's self is one's character or nature

explanation.surface: A spirit in a character who needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' drops S from SELF.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mischievous supernatural being is a sprite, a spirit.

clue.text: Across the Channel, yours truly sent swimming, wet

parts.note: across the Channel is France, where 'yours truly', me, is moi

indicators.note: swimming makes the letters of sent move around

explanation.surface: Someone sent to swim the Channel ends up wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges SENT to STEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen something slightly is to wet it.

clue.text: Sneakily move line, splitting team

indicators.note: the line letter splits the word for team in two

parts.note: a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A player sneaks along the line, dividing the team.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge furtively sideways is to move sneakily.

clue.text: Poem recalled US Civil War commander, one standing on bank?

indicators.note: recalled means the poem's title is called back, reading it backwards

parts.note: If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling
William Tecumseh Sherman was a Union general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A poem about a Civil War general standing on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money; here it is a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler often stands on a riverbank casting a line.
